renders_to: Rendered by docs/board/render-board.mjs into docs/board/rc-board.rendered.html, a gitignored build product that is generated and never hand-edited. That HTML is published as a claude.ai artifact at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/e346cb5b-cb39-42ce-aa14-821ceb53e4ce, and the same URL is re-rendered and updated after every board change so the owner link stays live. The renderer, its client runtime and its stylesheet are ported from the OsteoJP repo rather than written from scratch. This JSON remains the single source of truth: the render is strictly downstream of it and never writes back.
doctrine: A board claim is never truth on its own. The evidence field carries the proof. The executor terminal (ORANGE) updates this JSON at every checkpoint. A card may not enter status=shipped with evidence=null; a launch gate condition may not be state=pass with evidence=null. Enforced by docs/board/validate-board.mjs, which must exit 0 before any checkpoint is considered recorded. GATE VOCABULARY: green_self_merge means ORANGE self-decides, commits locally, proceeds without approval. owner_merge means the card closes only on Ivan confirming the deployed screen on localhost, a local commit alone never closes it. stakeholder means client acceptance at phase end. cyan_clear and owner_authorizo are unused in this project. EVIDENCE VOCABULARY: kind journal is a local commit sha or command output pasted so a stranger can re-verify, kind screenshot is Ivan on-screen confirmation. PHASE 1 REALITY: no remote, no CI, no credentials exist in phase 1; the executor updates this JSON at every checkpoint. Every card is built and verified on localhost only, and every commit is local. ORANGE self-decides all creative and code-level questions and halts only on an absolute blocker, in which case the card moves to status=halted or status=blocked with blocked_on set and the reason written into notes.

cards.title: Next.js app scaffolded on localhost with Tailwind, folder structure, git initialized, zero external services.
cards.notes: Foundation card. Next.js App Router with TypeScript and Tailwind, running on localhost with one command, plus the folder structure the later cards fill in (routes, components, mock data module, shared UI). No Supabase, no env vars, no tokens, everything static, desktop-first only: this is a preview built to sell the vision and win a paid phase 2, not a system that stores anything. There is no database and no API layer at all; every screen reads from the in-repo mock module that RC-02 delivers. Deliberately not done: responsive/mobile layouts, auth, any persistence across reloads. Git is already initialized by YELLOW at the repo root and docs/board is already committed, so do not re-init the repository, just commit on top. ORANGE self-decides framework version, folder naming and component conventions.

cards.title: Mock data layer complete: products, batches, suppliers, inbound orders, outbound issues, statuses, reminders, plus two fabricated realistic order confirmation PDFs.
cards.notes: Every screen reads from this single module, so the data has to be believable before any screen is built: a demo dies on fake-looking data faster than on a missing feature. Products must match the client niche: bituminous shingle, metal roof tile, mineral wool, decorative plaster, klinker stone, drywall profiles, adhesives, rainwater systems. Each product carries SKU, name, category, one fixed unit of measure, a reorder threshold and current stock. Units are mixed on purpose across m2, lm, pcs, bag, kg, roll and m3, because the fixed-unit-per-product rule is part of what is being sold. Batches exist per inbound line and are created on arrival. Inbound orders are whole-order status only, Pending arrival or Arrived, with a supplier, a currency of EUR or RON, and an MDL field: currencies are EUR and RON with an MDL field, no live FX, so the MDL value is a stored number in the mock data, not a computed conversion. Outbound is issue-to-project and never a retail sale: client name, project name, quantities, optional sale price, status Awaiting shipment or Shipped. Projects are named like real ones, for example Acoperis Orhei 100m2, Fatada Costesti. Single warehouse, single user, no login. The two fabricated order confirmation PDFs are the upload fixtures for RC-04 and must look like real EU supplier confirmations. Deliberately not done: partial arrivals, partial shipments, multi-warehouse, any FX rate source.

cards.title: Dashboard renders total stock value, low-stock count, pending inbound, pending outbound and recent activity, all computed from the mock data.
cards.notes: Closes gate G2. This is the landing screen and the first thing the client sees, so the five blocks have to be readable at a glance: total stock value, count of products under their reorder threshold, count of inbound orders still Pending arrival, count of outbound issues still Awaiting shipment, and a recent activity feed. Every number is derived from the RC-02 mock data at render time rather than hardcoded on the page, so the figures stay consistent with what the other screens show. Low stock is defined as current stock at or below the product reorder threshold. Stock value is summed in a single display currency; ORANGE picks it and labels it, using the stored MDL field rather than converting anything. Gate is owner_merge: a local commit does not close this card, Ivan confirming the screen on localhost does.
cards.open_on_purpose: Work is complete and committed, but the gate is owner_merge: RC-03 closes only when Ivan confirms the dashboard on localhost during the review wave. A local commit does not ship it.

cards.title: Upload Order flow works end to end: upload zone, simulated AI processing animation, prefilled editable review form, confirm.
cards.notes: Closes gate G3. This is the money screen, it sells the preview, give it the most polish: more time goes here than on any other card. The AI is simulated with a scripted delay and prefilled values from mock data, using the two fabricated confirmation PDFs from RC-02 as the upload fixtures. Nothing is parsed and nothing is sent anywhere; the file is accepted, a processing animation runs on a timer with visible stages so it reads as work being done, and the review form then appears already filled with supplier, currency, dates and line items. The review form is fully editable: the operator can correct any field, add or remove a line, then confirm, and the order lands in the inbound list as Pending arrival. Drag-and-drop plus click-to-browse both work. ORANGE self-decides the animation timing, staging copy and micro-interactions. Deliberately not done: real OCR, real extraction, any upload to a server.

cards.title: Inventory management table filters by product, category, supplier and stock level, with per-product drill-down showing batches and movements.
cards.notes: Closes gate G5. This is the screen the warehouse actually lives in, so it has to survive being clicked around rather than just looked at. All four filters work against the mock data and can be combined: product (search by name or SKU), category, supplier, and stock level (for example all, low stock, out of stock). Rows show SKU, name, category, unit, current stock and threshold, with low-stock rows visually marked. Clicking a row opens a per-product detail view listing that product's batches (from inbound arrivals, with quantity and arrival date) and its movement history (inbound in, outbound out, with the project the material went to). Single warehouse, so there is no location column. ORANGE self-decides table layout, whether the drill-down is a page or a panel, and sort behaviour.

cards.title: Outbound form issues materials to a client project via searchable dropdowns with quantity and optional price.
cards.notes: Closes gate G6. Outbound here is issue-to-project, not a retail sale, and the form has to read that way: client name, project name, then the materials being sent to that site. Product and project pickers are searchable dropdowns because the catalogue is long and typing beats scrolling in a demo. Quantity is required and shown in the product's fixed unit; sale price is optional and clearly optional, because Rapid Construct often issues material to its own job without pricing it. Submitting creates an outbound issue with status Awaiting shipment. Deliberately not done: partial shipments, stock reservation logic, credit notes.
cards.open_on_purpose: Work is complete and committed, but the gate is owner_merge: RC-07 closes only when Ivan confirms on localhost that he can pick a client and project from searchable dropdowns, add products with quantities, leave the price blank or fill it, and submit.

cards.title: Order lifecycle board shows inbound and outbound columns with status chips and per-order status history.
cards.notes: Closes gate G7. One screen showing both directions of movement: inbound orders with Pending arrival and Arrived, outbound issues with Awaiting shipment and Shipped, each carrying a status chip in the design-system colours. Opening an order shows its lines and its status history as timestamped entries, which is what makes the lifecycle legible rather than just a label. Moving an inbound order to Arrived is what creates its batches, and that link should be visible in the UI even though the data is mock. Whole-order statuses only, partial arrivals and partial shipments are deliberately phase 2, record that as deliberately not done: if the client asks during the demo, the answer is that it is scoped for phase 2, not that it was forgotten.
cards.open_on_purpose: Work is complete and committed, but the gate is owner_merge: RC-08 closes only when Ivan confirms on localhost that inbound and outbound sit side by side with status chips and that opening an order shows its status history.

cards.title: Reminders screen shows per-product threshold setup and a fired-alerts list with email/SMS toggles as UI only.
cards.notes: Closes gate G8. Two halves on one screen: threshold setup, where every product shows its reorder threshold and current stock and the threshold can be edited, and a fired-alerts list showing alerts that have already triggered, with the product, the level that tripped them and when. Email and SMS toggles are UI only: nothing is sent, no provider exists, no credentials exist in phase 1, and the toggles must not imply otherwise in their labels. Keep the alerts list populated from mock data so the screen is not empty during the demo, since an empty state here reads as a broken feature. Deliberately not done: any delivery channel, any scheduling, any notification history beyond the mock list.

cards.title: Full click-through QA passed and demo route prepared for the owner review wave.
cards.notes: Last card before review. Two outputs: a full click-through of every screen and every control with the findings written down, and a prepared demo route, meaning the exact click order to walk a client through the story (dashboard, upload an order, review and confirm, see it inbound, mark arrived, issue material to a project, check inventory and reminders, settings). Fix what is trivially broken during the pass; anything larger becomes its own card rather than silently sliding. This card feeds the REVIEW BATCH (IVAN) lane; changes from review are handled in batch waves, never one-by-one interruptions, so ORANGE collects Ivan's feedback into cards in that lane and works the whole wave as one pass. Priority is medium rather than high because it cannot start until RC-00 through RC-10 exist.
